small_guidance:
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_N (256/512) paired with BLOCK_OC=32 and num_warps=8, plus a BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_OC=128 with num_stages=3-4 — current best likely underutilizes the 8192-element K=72 inner GEMM when BLOCK_OC is small.
- Reorder the program grid so pid_oc is axis 0 and pid_n is axis 1 (or add a swizzle/group-M scheme) to improve L2 reuse of the weight tile across spatial tiles in the same wave.
- Try BLOCK_K=128 (next pow2 of 72) with masking and use `tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` explicitly; also consider promoting the weight load to be tiled along K rather than fully loaded at once if larger BLOCK_OC is used.
large_guidance:
- Switch to NHWC (channels-last) input/weight layout so the GEMM-K (ic·kh·kw) dimension is contiguous: pre-permute weight to (KH,KW,IC,OC) once in __init__ and convert input to channels_last before the kernel. This removes the strided gather along stride_xc inside the inner loop and dramatically improves coalescing.
- Make the K loop explicit: tile over BLOCK_K=32 chunks of the 72-element reduction with an accumulator (instead of one giant BLOCK_K=128 load), which lets BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N grow (e.g. 128×128) without exploding register/shared usage, and enables software pipelining via num_stages=3-4.
- Consider a persistent-kernel + spatial-tile schedule: one program per (OC-tile, batch) that streams across OH×OW tiles, reusing the weight tile in registers across many output pixels — weights (64×72=4608 floats) easily fit and are reused B×OH×OW times.
